cards.subject: The Council of Tirisfal
lines: A secret order of mages took its name from these glades thousands of years ago, and appointed the Guardians.
Aegwynn was the second to last. Medivh was the last. This was a name in wizard history long before it was a graveyard.

cards.subject: The Mindless Ones
cards.tag: The same graveyard you woke in
lines: Every Forsaken starts among open coffins.
The things shambling around those graves came up out of the same ground and never got their minds back.
You are the exception, not the rule.

cards.subject: They are in the starting area
lines: There are living, armed Scarlet Crusaders inside the newbie zone, hunting the newly risen before they can get their names back.
They were deleted from the modern game.
In here, somebody is trying to kill you five minutes after you stand up.

cards.subject: Invincible's grave
lines: The Balnirs bred Lordaeron's white horses. Young Arthas played here, and was there when the colt was born.
When it died in a riding accident he buried it on the farm. The plaque is still readable.
The grave is open, and it is empty. He came back with Frostmourne and raised his horse.

cards.subject: Agamand Mills
cards.tag: The son who opened the gate
lines: The patriarch refused to run. He fortified the mills and talked his workers into staying.
His youngest son killed the watchmen in the night and let the Scourge in. A third of the defenders died in the first assault.
He is still there, as a skeletal mage. So is the commander who moved into the family crypt and raised their ancestors to fight them.

cards.subject: The Mass Graves
cards.tag: A named place on the map
lines: When the plague swept Tirisfal, the bodies went into pits, and the pits are labelled.
The gnolls crawling over it are animated by an embalming fluid made with warlock and necromantic magic together.
Somebody invented that fluid on purpose.

cards.subject: Thule Ravenclaw
lines: The Rot Hide are not simply plague victims. Their animating fluid was invented by a mage who betrayed his colleagues to join the Scourge.
He can lay his own curse on you.
The thread that starts by scraping ichor off gnolls at the pits ends with you killing him a zone away.

cards.subject: What the Monastery was
lines: It was a cathedral of the Church of the Holy Light, with real libraries and a seminary for paladins in training.
The Silver Hand took it back after the Third War as a forward base. It became the Scarlet Monastery only after that order splintered.
People who farmed all four wings for a year never learn that the Library was a library.

cards.subject: Whispering Gardens
lines: A great battle was fought on this hill between the Scourge and the men who became the Scarlet Crusade.
The fallen can still be heard, faintly, at twilight.
That is what the place is called and that is what it is.

cards.subject: Nightmare Vale
lines: Darkhounds and vampire bats have eaten the native wildlife out of this valley entirely.
There is a rare white bat living in it.
It is the only colour in a place that has none.

cards.subject: The sky
lines: Eternally gloomy and tinted a blighted green, with the flora clinging to its last shreds of life.
It is a deliberate colour cast over the whole zone rather than a passing storm.
Stand at the lake and look up.

cards.subject: The Bulwark
cards.tag: A pile of debris and a road
lines: A makeshift wall stacked along the border to turn back wandering undead. It was never meant to survive an assault.
The Forsaken and the Argent Dawn cooperate here, which they do almost nowhere else.
This zone is levels one to ten. The one on the other side is fifty-one to fifty-eight. There is no gate.
